title: Living Your (Best) Life With Wallets: Kolawole
body_markdown:
For the September episode of Live Your Best Life With Wallets, we spoke to Kolawole Sholabi. Kolawole is an electrical engineer living and working in Lagos.


When he’s not working, he follows football leagues ardently ( *and we’re sure he’s fixed to football szn and has probably joined the Wallets Nation FPL league*[here](https://fantasy.premierleague.com/leagues/auto-join/wj0hwy) )


**Nice to have you Kolawole. How did you find out about us?**


It wasn’t planned. I remember looking through my Twitter timeline on a particular day when I saw a tweet about traditional banks and the trauma that customers go through. I could relate so I kept reading the comments and just down there, someone mentioned Wallets Africa. So I took time to go through the Wallets Twitter page to understand how it works and I was impressed.


**So, what happened next?**


I created an account and now I use the app for my online transactions and I’m yet to experience any challenges.


**What was the convincing factor for you?**


The positive feedback I saw on Twitter was all it took to get me started on the product.


**Nice! And what will you say is your favourite feature on the app?**


The virtual dollar card. And that’s because it’s so easy to pay for transactions online without the typical limitations of the normal card.


**What features would you like to see on the app?**


It’ll be great to have a physical card linked to my account so that I can withdraw money or use it to pay for goods and services.


*(Editor’s note: Kolawole sent this in before our naira cards were launched! So if you haven’t requested yours yet,*[here’s a quick guide on how to do that](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-Pg9ZZahr_8) *)*


**If you had a million naira in your Wallets account and you had to finish it in 48 hours, what are you spending it on?**


Investments! I’ll invest N750,000 into a minor risk investment that has a good return. I’ll spend N150,000 on importation of phone accessories for my customers. And then, I’ll use the balance for upkeep.


*Interesting, so 75% to investments and just 10% for upkeep* .


Thank you so much to Kolawole for sharing your Wallets Africa experience. We enjoy reading from people like you and we’re indeed glad that we’re doing something right. Also, shout out to all the amazing people who keep sharing the good news of Wallets. It’s because of you that people like Kolawole are with the #WalletNation!
